title: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI
abstract: arXiv:2611.06830v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Current generative AI alignment relies on a myopic paradigm that prioritizes immediate conversational satisfaction. By relying on short-horizon feedback, this approach ignores the profound, longitudinal externalities of persistent human-AI interaction, which can lead to adverse outcomes such as cognitive atrophy, social erosion, and diminished human agency. To address this, we propose a paradigm shift toward long-horizon alignment that accounts for how AI reshapes human experience over time. To this end, we map the tensions between near-term utility and long-term costs of AI use across four facets of human well-being to reveal outcomes that current reward models fail to capture. Ultimately, we advocate for moving beyond simple preference optimization toward alignment strategies that actively foster long-term human well-being by navigating these complex temporal scales.

translated_abstract: 当前的生成式AI对齐依赖于一种短视的范式，即优先考虑即时对话满意度。由于依赖短程反馈，这种方法忽视了持续人机交互所带来的深远纵向外部性，可能导致认知萎缩、社会侵蚀以及人类能动性减弱等不良后果。为解决这一问题，我们提出向长程对齐的范式转变，即考量AI如何随时间重塑人类体验。为此，我们在人类福祉的四个维度上刻画了AI使用的近期效用与长期成本之间的张力，以揭示当前奖励模型未能捕捉的结果。最终，我们倡导超越简单的偏好优化，转向能够驾驭这些复杂时间尺度、积极促进人类长期福祉的对齐策略。
tldr: 该论文揭示了当前生成式AI对齐的“近视”缺陷——过度追求即时对话满意度而忽视长期负面影响（如认知萎缩与能动性减弱），并提出转向长程对齐范式，在人类福祉四个维度上权衡近期效用与长期成本。
en_tdlr: This paper exposes the "alignment myopia" of current generative AI—prioritizing immediate conversational satisfaction while overlooking long-term harms—and proposes a paradigm shift toward long-horizon alignment that balances near-term utility against long-term costs across four facets of human well-being.
